newsitem.title: USA: San Antonio plans $150 mln commercial paper sale.
newsitem.headline: San Antonio plans $150 mln commercial paper sale.

text.p: San Antonio's City Public Services Department plans to sell an additional $150 million in commercial paper this week to retire some long-term bonds maturing in the next seven years, officials said Monday.

The department also is looking to restructure its debt to reduce interest costs, maintain flexibility and remain competitive in an environment of electric utility deregulation expected in the years ahead, Assistant Treasurer Patricia Major said.

The department, which oversees the city's electric and water utilities, expects to save about $9 million in interest costs by retiring bonds with average interest rates between 5.5 percent and 6 percent that mature between 1998 and 2004, she said. The short term commercial paper expiring in 270 days will carry an interest rate of about 4 percent.

The $150 million issue is in addition to an existing $300 million commercial paper program. About $20 million is left over from that program, raising the total amount available for retiring the bonds to $170 million, Major said.

Typically, cities issue short-term securities like commercial paper to retire long-term debt that carries higher interest costs. Generally, the percentage of commercial paper outstanding to total debt is kept within 20 percent to maintain ratings.

Standard & Poor's has affirmed its A1+ rating on San Antonio's outstanding electric and water system commercial paper, reflecting the long term AA ratings on the bonds. The rating agency says the city's total variable rate exposure, including the $150 million commercial paper sale will remain at a manageable 18 percent of its total $2.5 billion of outstanding debt.
